title: Can Current SDS Controllers Scale To Modern HPC Infrastructures?
problem: Modern supercomputers face I/O interference and performance degradation as numerous jobs compete for shared storage resources. Software-defined storage solutions exist to coordinate storage through QoS policies but often fail to scale to modern HPC infrastructure sizes.
motivation: Determining whether current SDS solutions can effectively scale to manage modern supercomputer storage systems is critical for maintaining I/O performance at scale.
method: The researchers tested two different organizational structures for storage control on the Frontera supercomputer. One is flat (all nodes communicate directly with central control), the other is hierarchical (organized in layers, like a tree). As they added more computers to the system, they measured how well each design kept up with requests and at what point each one became too slow to be useful.
key_novelty: This is the first time anyone measured how flat versus hierarchical storage control designs actually perform when scaled to a real, working supercomputer.
contributions: First experimental study of SDS controller scalability limits on production HPC infrastructure
Evaluation showing flat design controllers scale to 2,500 nodes with 41ms average control cycle latency
Evaluation showing hierarchical designs scale to 10,000 nodes with 69-103ms average latency
Insights into advantages and shortcomings of state-of-the-art SDS solutions

metrics.other: flat design: 41ms latency at 2,500 nodes; hierarchical design: 69-103ms latency at 10,000 nodes

limitations: Scalability limitations of different design approaches not addressed beyond empirical observations
